text:
sylvie: Rolling up quokka13b-int6x to canary on p100-40g pool. Using per-layer int6 with fp16 residuals. Canary flags: microbatch=6, max_new_tokens=1800, kv_prefetch=aggressive. After ~10m we hit repeated OOMs and GPU slot churn. tagging @rick for allocator/insight and @anita for quant calibration notes

rick: saw the traces, looks like many small frees leaving unusable fragments. allocator slabs show lots of 64-256KB holes that never coalesce. any concrete log snippet?

sylvie: paste from one OOM incident:

```
[ERROR] alloc_failed: wanted 384MB (kv-cache)
[WARN] slab_allocator: free_chunk coalescer failed: adjacent_in_use=true
[kv] header_count=214748, header_overhead=1.8GB
serving: microbatch=6 seq=2300 peak_gpu=28.7GB
```

sylvie: header_count seems off — huge header blowup between warmup and steady state. multiple concurrent long-gen requests (>=1200) seem to amplify it.

anita: int6 calibration note: during quant we store per-layer scale tables in headers for faster dequant. quokka13b-int6x used a dense header layout to speed up lookup; that exploded when we enabled aggressive prefetch (it prefetches future KV headers too). two quick ideas: 1) switch header layout to sparse+varint to reduce header footprint, 2) limit prefetch depth for models with >10 layers.

rick: operational mitigations we can flip without binary change: - set microbatch=3 - clamp max_new_tokens=1024 - runtime flag kv_header_sparse=true - set prefetch_depth=3 for quokka template. That should cut header growth and reduce fragmentation.

sylvie: applying runtime flags now and spinning up a new canary. will also set slot_compactor.tail_slop=16KB to be more aggressive on small frees.

bench-robot: pre-change metrics from failing canary (6m window): p50=240ms p95=890ms tokens/s=150 mem_frag=0.78 header_size=1.8GB requeues=12

infra-bot: canary deploy note: quokka13b-int6x -> p100-40g (canary-7) at 2026-03-03T09:12:00Z

sylvie: post-change: ran 300 long-context evals (seq ~2100) with new flags. No OOMs in 45m. header_size reduced to 420MB. mem_frag=0.39. Perf delta: p50=280ms p95=920ms tokens/s=132.

anita: good. followups: 1) add sparse header layout in runtime (small lib change) to make this permanent 2) add a quant calibration step that emits header compacting metadata (we can drop redundant scale entries) 3) document quokka13b template defaults: max_new_tokens=1024, microbatch map: short<512->8, mid512-1024->6, long>1024->3, prefetch_depth<=3 for int6 variants.

rick: opened infra ticket to schedule slab coalescer work and compactor improvements: https://infra/ticket/SLAB-2042. Also PR for runtime flagging tests: https://phab/review/CR-9899

bench-robot: queued LVQA + fairness reg sets against quokka13b-int6x with sparse headers and new defaults. Will attach quality diffs to SLAB-2042.

sylvie: creating onboarding note for model template changes and recommended defaults: https://planner/ML-QUOKKA-TUNING. Marking thread as monitoring. Reopen if we see regressions after sparse header rollout. thanks :sparkles:
